stem: A pair of tangents are drawn to a unit circle with centre at the origin and these tangents intersect at A enclosing an angle of \(60^{\circ}\). The area enclosed by these tangents and the area of the circle is
_note: Three printed defects on this stem. (1) The degree symbol is dropped: the book prints 'an angle of 60 .' — restored here as 60 degrees. (2) The book prints the misspellings 'cnetre' (for centre) and 'tangetns' (for tangents); corrected here. (3) Mathematically consequential: the book asks for the area enclosed by these tangents and 'the area of the circle', which is meaningless as printed; it should read 'the ARC of the circle'. With the arc reading, OA = 2, tangent length = sqrt(3), kite area = sqrt(3), central angle POQ = 120 deg so sector area = pi/3, giving sqrt(3) - pi/3 = option B. Transcribed as printed.
solution: [Textbook misprints in the stem (three, one of them substantive). The angle is printed as an angle of \(60\) followed by a full stop, the degree symbol having been dropped; it is restored above as \(60^{\circ}\). The book also misspells centre as cnetre and tangents as tangetns. Substantively, the stem asks for the area enclosed by these tangents and the area of the circle, which names no well-formed region; it must read the ARC of the circle, that is, the region bounded by the two tangent segments and the minor arc joining their points of contact. The option set confirms that reading uniquely: it gives \(\sqrt{3} - \frac{\pi}{3} = 0.6849\), the keyed option, against \(0.6311\), \(0.7585\) and \(0.8252\) for the other three. The answer above follows the intended reading.]
